My home router is busted and the wifi no longer work so I use a hard line when I use this laptop. One day wanted to have an outing only to discover gasp that for reason unknown to me, I was not detecting any networks wifi networks nor did network manager give me any options to create them. Now this is a dual boot installation because this laptop is still under warranty....but...I know for sure that the hardware is fine because it works when I boot into the godless mess that is windows 10. At least I know that my wifi is controlled by a Qualcomm Atheros wifi/bluetooth network adapter. So I mounted my trusty duck and set about on the internets to search for answers.

The first promising answer was found on askubuntu.com by user Pilot6:

The device is supported in Ubuntu 15.10 with the latest updates.

  • You can get it to work in Ubuntu 14.04 by installing kernel 4.2 and update firmware. Run in terminal (Ctrl+alt+t for you noobs).
sudo apt-get install linux-generic-lts-wily
wget https://mirrors.kernel.org/ubuntu/pool/main/l/linux-firmware/linux-firmware_1.157_all.deb
sudo dpkg -i linux-firmware_1.157_all.deb
  • In Ubuntu 15.10 and later you only need to install the firmware:
sudo apt-get install linux-firmware

In both cases, reboot afterwards.

So I doed it and whalla! My network manager now allows me to create wifi connections.. I try to connect but **Y U no detect available networks?!" Well, shit..

I resaddled my ducks and headed back to the net. I needed to check the status of my network to begin troubleshooting why my fix no work. In the terminal I entered:

lshw -C network

...and the first line was about 'network UNCLAIMED'. What does this mean? Internets say this means my driver is missing for this network device. Internet also say that this is known issues with Atheros wifi cards and linux distros. I got stuck after this for a few days. I was unable to find anything that wasn't 3 years old. Le_complain....le_giveup.

Today I decided to give it another shot. I forget where but I found:

sudo apt-get install build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r) git
 echo "options ath10k_core skip_otp=y" | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/ath10k_core.conf
 wget https://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/projects/backports/stable/v4.4.2/backports-4.4.2-1.tar.gz
 tar -zxvf backports-4.4.2-1.tar.gz
 cd backport-4.4.2-1
 make defconfig-wifi
 make
 sudo make install
 git clone https://github.com/kvalo/ath10k-firmware.git
 sudo cp -r ath10k-firmware/QCA9377 /lib/firmware/ath10k/
 sudo cp /lib/firmware/ath10k/QCA9377/hw1.0/firmware-5.bin_WLAN.TF.1.0-00267-1 /lib/firmware/ath10k/QCA9377/hw1.0/firmware-5.bin

Mind you I have no idea what this does. I think it compiles a new kernel with backported drivers. I gave the old laptop a reboot after this and now it seems to be working. However, I have not tested the long term stability of the connections or signal strength.

One more thing....apparently if you update your kernel you will break this fix so you have to enter:

 cd backports-4.4.2-1
 make clean
 make defconfig-wifi
 make
 sudo make install

...and this should get it working.

Kays that's all I got. Hope this helps some other noob.
